Invisible Physics — Interactive 360° 3D & 2D Visualization Lab

True WebGL 3D Models: Left-click & drag any plot to rotate in 3D, scroll to zoom, right-click to pan, and hover to inspect exact SI values.

How to Interact with These 3D Models:
• Rotate in 3D: Hold down your Left Mouse Button on any 3D surface and drag in any direction.
• Zoom In / Out: Roll your Mouse Scroll Wheel up or down over the plot.
• Inspect Values: Hover your cursor over the 3D surface to see exact $(x, y, V)$ coordinates and green 2D equipotential contour projections!

Physical Interpretation: The positive charge ($+1.5\ \mu\text{C}$, red peak) creates a steep electrostatic potential hill ($V > 0$), while the negative charge ($-1.5\ \mu\text{C}$, blue well) creates a deep potential well ($V < 0$). Notice the green equipotential contour rings projected onto the bottom/top planes as you hover!

Physical Interpretation: Four alternating charges ($+q, -q, +q, -q$) form two positive peaks and two negative valleys meeting at a central saddle point $(0, 0)$ where both $V = 0$ and $|\mathbf{E}| = 0$.

Physical Interpretation: Two equal positive charges ($+1.5\ \mu\text{C}, +1.5\ \mu\text{C}$) create twin potential hills separated by a elevated saddle pass at $(0, 0)$ where $V > 0$ but the slope vanishes ($\mathbf{E} = -\nabla V = \mathbf{0}$).

Physical Interpretation: Rotate this 3D electromagnetic wave to view it along the $x$-axis (head-on) and confirm that the red electric field $\mathbf{E}_y(x, t)$ and blue magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_z(x, t)$ oscillate at exactly $90^\circ$ to each other and to the propagation axis!
